result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A shows all 12 sailings in a compact, clean table on desktop. Fares are right-aligned, routes stay on one line, and the zebra striping and bold departure/route text make each row easy to scan. B wraps its routes awkwardly in a narrow column and left-aligns the fares. It also bolds Arrives and Bikes, which competes with the departure time, and not all rows fit in the view. Neither screenshot shows the phone layout, so item 3 is scored on what can be inferred. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B's table scans more cleanly on desktop: each sailing fits on one line, fares are right-aligned, and departure times and routes stand out because Arrives is not bold. A wraps its routes onto two lines and makes Arrives as bold as Departs, so the rows are taller and the departure time is less prominent. The screenshots show neither page's markup or a phone-width view, so I gave both a middle score on mobile readiness; B's data is also more consistent, for example the same boat's connecting sailings line up.
